question: Apart from reports with no identifiable failure mode, which failure mode is most common for pacemakers (LWP)?
answer:
**Lead capture (pacing not reaching the heart)** is the most common failure mode for pacemakers once the "no identifiable failure mode / other" group is set aside. It accounts for 7,673 reports, a 20.5% share of all 37,413 LWP reports in 2022–2024 [failure_modes tool, LWP, 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31].

- Its definition covers high or low impedance, loss of capture, high threshold, lead dislodgement or fracture, and header or connection problems.
- The next most common modes are battery (7,387 reports, 19.7%) and infection/pocket (4,515, 12.1%).
- The 20.5% share is measured against all reports, including the 11,383 (30.4%) in the excluded group, so it is not a share of the remaining reports.
- The codebook agrees with reference labels on about 70% of test reports, so some of these mappings may be off.
- A high count reflects reports received, not a failure rate, since the tool has no count of pacemakers in use. Larger manufacturers also file more reports.
